checks.detail: OptimizerGeneric returns success=True with message 'CONVERGENCE: RELATIVE REDUCTION OF F <= FACTR*EPSMCH' after 4 iterations and 924 function evaluations, leaving the merit at 5.417136e+00 against its starting 2.749850e+00 -- 1.97x WORSE. maxiter 60, 200 and 500 all stop at the same point, so this is convergence, not truncation. A freeform tilted-mirror merit function is not smooth (rays vignette in and out as surfaces move), so the finite-difference gradient is unreliable. res.success is not evidence: compare the merit before and after.
checks.name: the_optimizer_reports_success_while_making_the_design_worse

checks.detail: 0 of 27 variables outside their bounds: the degradation is a genuine interior point of the feasible set, not a bounds-handling bug
checks.name: the_bad_step_stays_inside_the_declared_bounds

checks.detail: local-frame chief-ray image heights after optimization: axial +0.8737 mm (target +0.0000), plus +2.5692 mm (target +2.6186), minus -0.8390 mm (target -2.6186). Only the +1.5 deg field reaches its f*tan(theta) target; the axial and -1.5 deg fields do not, consistent with the optimizer having stopped at a worse point than it started.
checks.name: the_other_two_intercept_targets_are_missed_and_the_gap_is_recorded

checks.detail: mean RMS spot radius over the three fields 0.112391 -> 0.095020 mm (1.18x), measured by direct traces rather than through the operands. A converged anastigmat design would be orders better; this is what the failed optimization leaves behind.
checks.name: the_mean_rms_spot_does_not_improve_by_the_order_of_magnitude_a_working_run_would

checks.detail: mirror 3 is decentered by -14.9982 mm and the chief ray crosses it at global y = -14.6121 mm, so a global-frame intercept operand would be offset by order 15.0 mm from the local one. 'real_y_intercept_lcs' measures in the surface's own frame, which is the only frame in which 'centre the mirror on its chief ray' means anything.
checks.name: the_lcs_suffix_is_load_bearing_on_a_decentered_mirror

checks.detail: max |y(lambda) - y(0.587 um)| = {'0.486': 0.0, '0.587': 0.0, '0.656': 0.0}: identically zero at all three wavelengths. With no refractive surface there is no dispersion to have, and no amount of optimization can introduce any -- a physics invariant, not a tolerance.
checks.name: an_all_reflective_system_is_exactly_achromatic
